habitat: Dry bushveld, broad-leaved woodland, particularly mopane, and thornveld. It prefers drier conditions than Southern Yellow-billed Hornbill and forages mostly on open ground. Pairs and small flocks.
summary: A common pied hornbill identified by the red bill and the black-and-white chequered upperparts. The immature has a shorter bill and buff spots on the upperparts. The call is very like the Southern Yellow-billed Hornbill’s, but faster. No sourced Kruger population estimate is published for this species, and that gap was left as it is.

similar.note: Southern Yellow-billed Hornbill has a large yellow bill and a similar call given more slowly. It prefers less dry woodland.
Crowned Hornbill has a red bill too, but plain brown upperparts and a yellow bill base, and it stays in forest rather than open mopane.

population.notes: No sourced Kruger estimate is currently available; taxonomy or later records require separate research.

head.pattern: Pied, with a bright red bill.

viewNotes.note: Red bill and chequered black-and-white upperparts, usually on open ground.
The bright red bill is the front mark.
Chequered upperparts, not the plain brown back of a Crowned Hornbill.
Chequered upperparts in flight. A separate upperwing colour was not named.
White underparts from the pied pattern. The underwing was not named separately.

calls.description: Very difficult to tell from the Southern Yellow-billed Hornbill, but given more rapidly. The texts do not separate the sexes. Grade A from Temba, Gauteng. The filename is rbill1.

research.note: Status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Newman calls it a common resident. There is no Kemp estimate, and the empty population was left unchanged. Chick down beyond the shorter bill and buff spots, and a flight photograph, are gaps. The call is grade A from Gauteng. The photograph is CC0.
